learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will learn to draft formal printed invitations, formal replies (acceptance/refusal), and informal personal invitations while understanding the distinct tone and format differences.]
warm_up_hook: 💌 Hosting a grand gala or a cozy pizza party? The way you invite people sets the whole vibe! Let's master the etiquette of invitations so your guests know exactly what to expect. 🎩

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Used for large gatherings like weddings, annual days, or inaugurations. They are written in the third person (He/She/They/The Principal). The sentences are broken into multiple lines and center-aligned. It ends with RSVP on the bottom left.
examples_or_templates: Standard phrasing: 'Mrs. & Mr. Sharma request the pleasure of your benign presence on the auspicious occasion of...'
RSVP: Respondez s'il vous plait (Please reply).

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Replies must be prompt and match the tone of the invitation. Written in the third person. If refusing, you must state a polite, valid reason (e.g., prior commitment) and wish them well for the event.
examples_or_templates: Acceptance: 'Mr. Gupta thanks Mr. Sharma for the kind invitation and has great pleasure in accepting it.'
Refusal: '...regrets his inability to attend due to a prior engagement. Wishes the couple a happy married life.'

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Used for friends and close relatives. These follow the format of an informal letter (Sender's Address, Date, Salutation). They are written in the first and second person (I/You) with a warm, casual tone.
examples_or_templates: Informal Invite: 'Dear Amit, I am hosting a small dinner party to celebrate my promotion...'
Informal Refusal: 'Dear Rahul, Thank you so much for inviting me, but I'll be out of town that weekend...'

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ In which person is a formal printed card invitation written?
❓ What is essential when drafting a formal refusal to an invitation?
options: Stating a valid reason for absence.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: Stating a valid reason for absence.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Draft a formal printed invitation card on behalf of the Principal of Sunrise School for their upcoming Annual Sports Day.
subjective_practice.hint: Use center alignment, third person, include the Chief Guest's name, and add RSVP on the bottom left.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write a formal reply of refusal to the invitation created above.
subjective_practice.hint: Write as the invited guest in the third person (e.g., 'Dr. Rao thanks the Principal... but regrets his inability...').

activity_or_assignment.title: 🎭 The Dual Invite Challenge
activity_or_assignment.instructions: You are hosting a graduation party. Draft a formal invitation card for your teachers/professors, and then draft an informal letter invitation for your best friends. Notice the shift in tone and layout!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Formal Invitations (Cards) use the third person, center alignment, and include an RSVP.
⭐ Informal Invitations use the first/second person and follow an informal letter format.
⭐ Formal Refusals must politely state a reason (like 'prior commitment') in the third person.
